podcast.body: Elvis Presley's cover of this song was performed on the "Stage Show" TV program, notably airing simultaneously with Carl Perkins's own TV debut performing the song on "Ozark Jubilee." Initially, a "gentleman's agreement" prevented its release as a single to avoid competing with Perkins's sales, but it was included on Elvis's first album and an EP. When eventually released as a single later in the year, it reached the top 20 and generated additional royalties for Perkins. Elvis's rendition maintains a consistent 4/4 beat throughout and conveys a strong sense of "urgency," contrasting with Perkins's more rhythmically complex original. "Thresley was on stage show on another network, performing his cover version of it."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs
srcs.episode: Episode 36: "Blue Suede Shoes" by Carl Perkins

podcast.body: Elvis's cover version of this song was chosen by him for his first album and was described as a "fine performance" suitable for an album track, even if it didn't match the quality of the original. "while his versions of Blue Swade's shoes, or Tuti Fruity, didn't match the quality of the originals, they were fine performances and perfect for album tracks."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs
